TS-Pico 2.2 is firmware 2.2 with ROM 2.2. ROM 2.2 is ROM 2.1 with two small fixes. Firmware 2.2 also works with ROM 2.1, so a board on 2.1 can take the firmware alone and update the ROM later. Boards coming from 1.1 need both, and the web updater handles that.

**Coming from 1.1?** Read [What's new in the TS-Pico since 1.1](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updates/whats-new-since-1-1/).

## ROM 2.2

- **`tpi:tape` leaves the printer switch alone.** `tpi:picopt`, then `tpi:tape`, then `tpi:sdcard` used to send printing back to the 2068 without saying so, because `tpi:tape` turned both switches off. Now it changes only the LOAD/SAVE switch, like `tpi:sdcard`, `tpi:picopt` and `tpi:ts2040`. (#185)
- **`f:` files and `OPEN #` channels give Report J at once when no TS-Pico answers.** They used to wait for the full timeout first. (#205)
- `PRINT PEEK 101` gives **34** (22h), and the start-up line reads `2026 TS-Pico ROM v2.2`.

## Firmware fixes

Some of these change a message. Those messages appear only with VERBOSE on (`SAVE "tpi:verbose" CODE 1,1`); with it off you see just the report.


- **`tpi:blkrcv`** refuses with "No ROM image mounted" and Report F unless a `.ROM`, `.BIN` or `.DCK` is mounted. It used to answer "OK", and `romupdate` would go on to erase the slot. (#184)
- **`tpi:log`** on a new Pico, before anything has been logged, says "The log is empty" instead of Report J. A failed `tpi:log clear` is no longer reported as a success. (#186)
- **`tpi:dir CODE 1,n` / `2,n`** out of range: with VERBOSE on, the message gives the right last index ("0-11" for twelve files), and an empty folder says so. With VERBOSE off it is Report 6, as before. (#188)
- **`tpi:dock CODE 0,2`**, with VERBOSE on, names the setting it swapped to. (#189)
- **`tpi:newtap a.b.tap`** makes `a.b.tap`, not `a.b.tap.tap`. (#190)
- **`tpi:ffw CODE 2,n` / `3,n`** on the last file, with VERBOSE on, says "Can't FWD. No later file." instead of claiming it moved; it no longer lists the tape either. (#191)
- **`tpi:md`** takes its name like every other command, and refuses `.`, `..`, paths and names FAT can't hold. A leading `/` used to make the folder on the Pico's own flash. (#192)
- Long dotted paths in `CAT` listings are cut to the length asked for. (#193)
- A block-graphic or UDG character whose pattern arrives garbled is logged as a warning and printed anyway. (#201)
- No window at the start of a command in which the 2068 could read a stale READY, after `ERASE` with a prompt. (#204)
- Smaller fixes in code that nothing reaches today: an empty `PROMPT_EACH` (#194) and the parked ZX compatible-mode LOAD (#202).

## For programmers

The [programmer's reference](https://github.com/timex-sinclair-projects/tspico-firmware-build/tree/main/docs/reference) explains the firmware and the ROM function by function, and CI keeps it in step with the code. (#159, #187, #197)

## Testing

Each fix has a host test, and the two ROM fixes run in a Z80 interpreter from the committed image. The ACTIVATE_MQ fix (#204) rests on behaviour checked on a TS-Pico. The other fixes have not each been tried on a TS-Pico.

## Installing

1. **Switch the TS-2068 off.**
2. Open the [web updater](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updater/) in Chrome or Edge, connect the TS-Pico by USB, choose **Latest release**, and follow the steps.
3. **On a board already on 2.1**, the page updates only the firmware unless you tick **Update the TS-2068 ROM**. Tick it to get ROM 2.2. The ROM update erases the Pico's own files first and puts fresh ones back, so settings you changed in `config.ini` go back to their defaults. The SD card is not touched. Boards coming from 1.1 get the ROM update ticked for them.
4. Keep the **P10 jumper** fitted.

Afterwards, `SAVE "tpi:info"` shows firmware 2.2. `PRINT PEEK 101` gives **34** on ROM 2.2, or 33 if the board kept ROM 2.1.

## Downloads

- `firmware.uf2`: the TS-Pico firmware, for dragging onto the Pico's RPI-RP2 drive by hand.
- `upgrade.uf2`: the ROM updater.
- `Pico-v2.2.rom`: the whole 512K flash image.
- `pico_host-*.zip`: the TS-Pico firmware for emulators, for macOS, Linux and Windows. See `tools/emu/README.md`.
- The release zip: the firmware, the Pico's files, ROM 2.2 (`src/rom/TSPICO-22.ROM`) and the SD card files.
